chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Abi Khadija, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him)

that he used to sit the sitting of a slave, and place his hand on the ground, and eat with three fingers, and that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to eat like this, not as the tyrants do, one of them eating with his two fingers.

key_terms.جِلْسَةَ الْعَبْدِ: the sitting of a slave/servant (indicating humility)

ai.seo_question: How did the Prophet and Imams eat to demonstrate humility?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Prophetic sunnah of humility in daily acts, specifically contrasting the Imam’s servant-like posture and three-fingered eating with the ostentatious two-fingered style of 'tyrants' (al-jabbarun). It underscores the Shia emphasis on mirroring the Prophet’s modesty to reject arrogance, linking physical etiquette to spiritual character. The reference to 'tyrants' evokes the Quranic critique of those who consume wealth unjustly and act with haughtiness.
